notes: Side effect outside the issue: `hl_lines` (parsed to a list) was emitted as `hl_lines="[1, 2]"` (a Python repr) at base and is now dropped, both inside attr braces and in the legacy ```python hl_lines="1" form. This is arguably an improvement and no test pins the old output, but the changelog only mentions boolean options. Consider mentioning `hl_lines` in the changelog too.

docs/extensions/fenced_code_blocks.md 'Key/Value Pairs' section says key/value pairs are assigned as attributes when highlighting is off. A sentence noting that Pygments-only options (linenums, hl_lines, ...) are omitted would keep the docs accurate.

With codehilite enabled, bare `linenums` parses to None (because of preserve_none), so it doesn't turn on line numbers while `linenums="true"` does. That behaviour existed before this PR and is out of scope.
Pygments isn't installed in this environment, so the codehilite path was only checked in its no-Pygments fallback mode.
summary: The fix is minimal and in the right place, in the non-Pygments branch of FencedBlockPreprocessor.run: only string values are written as <code> attributes. Every case in the issue (bare linenums, linenums="true"/"false"/1, guess_lang, noclasses) now renders a plain code block. In a copy with the fix reverted, those same inputs raise the reported TypeErrors and the 3 new tests fail, so the tests do exercise the change. Other attributes (data-x, bare non-bool flags) are kept. Output without attr_list or with codehilite is unchanged. The full suite passes (1169 tests, 52 skipped), flake8 is clean, and a changelog entry is present. One side effect: the old `hl_lines="[1, 2]"` repr output is now dropped. That is acceptable but not mentioned in the changelog, so I've left it as a note.
